comment: S38b (spec §7 case 2: read back). The page reads as seven parts of 24,000 characters; every entry deploys its own 20-hex-digit commit. The final note, in the last part, names the commit that broke production; it was deployed at entry 1217, in part 3, a part the served link has summarized by the time she reads the last one on a 32k window. The summary is written before she learns which commit matters, and the part maps ~480 entries to their commits — more than twice the 5%-of-window cap a summary is written to — so a summary is unlikely to keep it. Passes only when she calls read_result (the marker names it) and names entry 1217. Re-reading the page (browser_read with a query) would find it too, and is red here by design: the case measures the read-back the spec asks for. The read_result clause declares the page's size (page_chars) and applies only when a round's llm_call span states a window too small to hold it (orchestrator ruling 2026-10-13): on a window that holds the page, or states none, she needs no read_result, the clause is not applicable and the right entry passes. guard_absent('narration') as the S38 browser cases. Added with the S38b corpus bump.
